apps.note: Fantasy football
apps.next: Nothing waiting on Jerry. He ran the Trade finder on his own league on 23 Nov and it was rebuilt twice on what he found, then the offer box was fixed. TRADE FINDER as it stands (v4.33; PRs #610, #612, #613, #614, #616, #618, #619, #620 and the v4.33 one). HELD TO HIS WRITE-UP since v4.33: he pasted "Fantasy Football Trade Analysis – Best Practices (Professional & Sharp Approach)" as the standard. Three things changed to meet it. A player's TRADE VALUE is his points above what the waiver wire offers at his position, so a quarterback scoring 18 is no longer the equal of a receiver scoring 18. The second player in a package counts three-quarters. A trade is EVEN when the two sides are within a tenth, or a point a week, replacing the old 30 percent. And the write-up says to ignore hot and cold streaks unless the role changed, so decision (2) below is UNDONE: his last four weeks no longer move his value, they are a buy-low or sell-high note on the card. WHAT THE WRITE-UP ASKS FOR THAT THE APP CANNOT DO, and says so in its footer: real-trade market values (FantasyCalc and the like), expert rest-of-season rankings, target and snap share, schedule strength. None of it is in what ESPN sends. Bringing in an outside source is his call, since it is third-party data inside an app that is sold, and it has not been asked of him yet. TWO THINGS DECIDED WITHOUT HIM in v4.32, because he said "Ok keep working on it. It needs some improvements" and left what to me. (1) A trade is now scored over the WEEKS LEFT in the season with each player worth nothing in his bye week, instead of one typical week; the card says "An average week over the N weeks left, bye weeks counted" and flags a bye still to come. To undo, say: "score trades on one week again, ignore byes". (2) A player's value leans 40 percent on his LAST FOUR WEEKS where ESPN sends them with the roster, and the card warns when he has cooled off or is running hot. To undo, say: "value players on the season average only". NOT CHECKABLE FROM A CLOUD CHAT: whether ESPN sends those weekly lines on his league. If it does, a row reads "last 3: 14.2"; if no row ever says "last", ESPN is not sending them and (2) is doing nothing, harmlessly. The finder, in Assistant Manager, ESPN leagues only. IT NOW COMES UP WITH THE IDEAS ITSELF (v4.31). He said: "You need to make this a smart algarithym it needs to gather information and and then make some decisions on what move is best for both teams, looking at the after trade analysis and see if projected scores are higher for both teams.. of if have an extra player or two and a team is short a player, then that is a potential good trade. Those are thoughts you need to be able to come up with". So, untouched, it weighs every one-for-one, two-for-one and one-for-two with every team (about ten thousand swaps), rebuilds both starting lineups for each, and shows the best three, one a manager, each with BOTH teams' best lineup before and after, what the other team is short of, and who each side still starts. Two-for-one is how his spare players reach a team that is short; nobody in a package is a throw-in, each has to start for the team that gets him. A proposal has to be worth a point a week to both lineups. Unasked it never brings in a player only at a position where he is already strong; a tap on QB, RB, WR or TE narrows it to that position. The paragraph that follows was written for v4.29 and still holds except where this one differs, in Assistant Manager, ESPN leagues only. IT NOW READS THE TEAM AND HE PICKS THE POSITION (v4.29, PR #616). He sent a picture of his roster, was told in chat his weakness was tight end, and said: "The trade finder should figure this out the way you just did. I'd like to tell you that I'd like to improve my rb position and then have you go find a potential trade that is a win win situation for both teams." So it opens on a four-line report, QB, RB, WR and TE against the league with rank, and what is healthy on the bench to trade from; under it, four buttons, "Which position do you want to improve?" Untouched it looks at his weakest; a tap looks where he says. Weak and strong are now a tenth of the league average at that position, not a flat two points, which is why a last-place tight end had never been called weak. THE RULES EVERY PROPOSAL STILL HAS TO PASS, from his own words on 23 Nov: quarterbacks, running backs, receivers and tight ends only, never kicker or defense; a player is valued on his points per game THIS season, and one who is out or on IR is worth nothing and is never offered; the two players must be within 30 percent in value; BOTH starting lineups must come out better, which is the win-win, and the other team must be no worse off at the position it gives from (his rule: "you can't propose a trade for a qb for instance if the other team doesn't have a good option"); and it is counted STARTER BY STARTER since v4.30 — shown "your best receiver for their best back" he said "You would only do that trade if i had at least two good wr", so after a swap every starting spot at the position given from must still hold a player as good as the league's average starter there, on both teams, and the card names who he still starts; nobody pays more than he gains; ranked by the worse-off side, one per manager, top three. If nothing passes it says so ("If a trade makes not sense, don't propose it"). It also shows the waiver wire and bye-week swaps. THE OFFER BOX IS NOT A PROPOSAL (v4.28, PR #614): the three dropdowns for checking an offer someone sent used to open on the first name in each list, his quarterback and theirs, right under "No trade makes sense right now", and he read it as a trade proposed to him. They open empty now and say it is not a suggestion. It adds no requests to ESPN and makes no live model call to decide anything; the AI only writes the message to send. Not built on purpose: 2-for-1 packages. NOT CHECKABLE FROM A CLOUD CHAT: ESPN is blocked from the container, so everything was proved on stand-in leagues and only his phone shows his real league. FOLLOW-UP OWNED BY THE TESTING CHATS, not this one: Assistant Manager gained a section, so the ff videos and testers/scripts/ff.json want a look; no existing video line changed, so nothing needed re-recording. Earlier the same evening, all confirmed on his phone: each player's NFL team badge on his roster row (v4.22, v4.23) and the team badge on the roster heading (v4.20, v4.21). The app still waits on Yahoo: the Yahoo worker is MERGED to main (PR #47, merged 27 Oct — it is not a draft) at _workers/ff-yahoo/, and is deliberately NOT deployed because Yahoo's Fantasy API is behind a manual review and the application sent 22 Oct has drawn only an automated acknowledgement; Jerry chased it by email on 16 Nov.
